architectural_units.description: The administrator is a user with additional permissions to assign or revoke access to applications.

architectural_units.name: Presentation Layer
architectural_units.description: The presentation layer receives requests and builds responses.

architectural_units.name: Business Logic Layer
architectural_units.description: The business logic layer applies the domain rules.

architectural_units.name: Data Access Layer
architectural_units.description: The data access layer interacts with the database.

architectural_units.name: Domain Layer
architectural_units.description: The domain layer defines the data model.

architectural_units.name: Contract Layer
architectural_units.description: The contract layer separates the internal model from the external representation of the API.

architectural_units.name: Leader
architectural_units.description: This microservice has as its main function the routing of all communications to the corresponding microservice within the system architecture.

architectural_units.name: Portal
architectural_units.description: The portal microservice has as its main function to offer a centralized interface for access to the different VWGS applications.

architectural_units.name: Access Control
architectural_units.description: The Access Control microservice has as its main objective the management of user authentication and their permissions within the application.

architectural_units.name: Communication Log
architectural_units.description: The Communication Log microservice has as its main purpose to record all communications that occur within the system.

architectural_units.name: Scheduler
architectural_units.description: This microservice has as its main function the planning and programming of processes within the system.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The application has an architecture based on microservices, which consists of dividing the system into a set of small, independent, and autonomous services where each microservice is responsible for a specific functionality.

patterns.name: Cloud Architecture
patterns.description: The application is designed, deployed, and executed using cloud services (cloud computing) instead of local or physical servers.

patterns.name: Client-Server
patterns.description: The application follows the Client-Server pattern which organizes the code into two differentiated components: the client, which formulates service requests, and the server, which receives, processes, and returns responses.

patterns.name: MVVM
patterns.description: Angular applies the MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) pattern, as its architecture is based on components and services.

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: Spring Boot organizes the code following the layered pattern with which responsibilities are separated: the presentation layer receives requests and builds responses, the business logic layer applies domain rules, the data access layer interacts with the database, and the domain layer defines the data model.
